chapter: Glaser, the Arcadia and bands of 1939-41
title: Sunday sessions in Chicago and drinking zombies
summary: Roy played Sunday gigs with Baby Dodds and Jimmy McPartland and drank zombies, and Shorty Sherock tried to get him drunk.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: time I was there I did Sunday gigs with Harry Lim, did some dances at the Sherman. That's when I played with...that picture you see in the magazines.
Yeah. Baby Dodds was on some of them, too, right?
Yeah. Jimmy McPartland. That's when I was drinking those zombies. You're not supposed to drink but one of them; I used to drink five of them.
That's a rum drink, isn't it?

Oh, no, you put a lot of things in there. You use rum, scotch, bourbon... It's just a conglomerate drink. That's why they call it a Zombie, you know. In fact, that was my lunch! Heh-heh. To keep from being hungry.

While I was working at the Capitol, Gee was in town, you know, and Shorty Sherock used to come around. And he used to try to make me drunk, you know. He would set up like ten drinks on the bar. I would drink all ten of them. He'd say, "Ten more," you know. But don't forget, there wasn't too much in them drinks either. In them clubs, you know, they don't put too much in the glass, especially if you're drinking by the shot. I was drinking supposedly
whiskey, Canadian Club... But you never could get me so drunk that I couldn't play my gig, you know.
